summary.text: 后 is an old graph used for a ruler and, in later received-text usage, a ruler’s principal wife. In simplified Chinese it also writes the separate word ‘after/behind’, represented by 後 in traditional Chinese. The graph’s early form is disputed; the evidence does not establish a component-by-component origin.

formation.text: The formation is disputed. The Shuowen account interprets 后 as a human figure issuing commands and analyzes it through 一 and 口; other reported analyses connect early forms with 司 or 毓. The evidence does not settle these accounts or establish the modern form as a picture of childbirth or a body part.

components.text: 口 is visible in the received graph. Shuowen includes it in its analysis, but the evidence does not establish it as an independently meaningful or pictorial component in the graph’s origin.

history.text: The evidence reports 后 with the sense ‘ruler’ in late Spring and Autumn bronze inscriptions. It also reports later received-text uses for a ruler’s principal wife; it does not establish a dated path between these senses or verify the earliest examples against primary inscriptions.

后 and 後 are reported as originally distinct graphs. In received texts, 后 was also used to write the word ‘after’; the proposed mechanism is that their spoken forms were alike or similar, not that ‘ruler’ developed into ‘after’. Both are pronounced hòu in modern Mandarin, but the evidence does not establish a same-system ancient sound comparison. Simplified Chinese later uses 后 as the written form for both words.

The account that oracle forms of 后 and 司 were the same graph, with orientation distinctions appearing in bronze forms, competes with a report that oracle 后 was written with 毓. Neither account supplies a settled graphic sequence for the received form.

uncertainties.text: The dossier does not settle the early graphic origin of 后 or establish a secure decomposition of its current form. Childbirth and rear-body interpretations are reported but are not supported by decisive paleographic evidence here.

The classical spelling use of 后 for 後 and the administrative details of their modern consolidation are reported through a search-result record whose target page could not be inspected. Their precise chronology therefore remains unresolved in this evidence.

senses.period: Late Spring and Autumn bronze inscriptions (reported; primary examples not independently verified)
senses.text: A late Spring and Autumn bronze use is reported with the sense ‘ruler’; the dossier does not securely date any earlier oracle use of the same graph and word.

senses.period: Received textual usage; transition date unresolved
senses.text: Received-text examples document 后 for a ruler’s principal wife. The evidence does not date a development from ‘ruler’ to this sense.

senses.period: Classical borrowing reported; precise chronology unresolved; current in simplified Chinese
senses.text: 后 writes the separate word ‘after/behind’ in simplified Chinese. This is described as a spelling borrowed for 後, rather than as a meaning that grew out of ‘ruler’; both graphs have modern Mandarin reading hòu, while an ancient same-system sound match is not established here.

developments.text: Both ruler and ruler’s principal wife are documented uses, but the evidence does not show when or through what semantic development one became the other.

The graph 后 was reused to write the distinct word represented by 後 because the words were reported to sound alike or similar. Modern Mandarin gives both hòu; the ancient sound match and the loan’s precise chronology are not established in the inspected evidence.

limitations.text: The dossier reports sense attestations and dictionary citations but does not establish a dated semantic chain from childbirth, succession, or ‘ruler’ to ‘empress’.

overview.text: 后 has been used for a ruler and a ruler’s principal wife. In simplified Chinese it also writes ‘after’: the separate graph 後 was borrowed for this word because the words were reported to sound alike or similar, though the ancient sound match is not established here.

components.text: 口 appears in the received graph and in Shuowen’s analysis, but its original role in 后 is unsettled.
